title: 공원 가기
intro: 설문에서 '공원 가기'를 고르면 자주 가는 공원 묘사 → 공원에서 하는 일·루틴 → 기억에 남는 경험 → 어릴 적 공원과 지금 비교가 자주 출제됩니다. 분당 집에서 걸어서 15분 거리인 중앙공원 하나를 정해 두고, 주말 가족 산책·아이들 자전거·평일 저녁 혼자 걷는 휴식을 모든 질문에 연결하세요. 비교 질문은 '대전에서 자랄 때의 작은 흙 놀이터 vs 지금 분당의 큰 공원'으로 고정하면 쉽게 답할 수 있습니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one.' 같은 시작 문장 → 공원 이름·위치(집에서 걸어서 15분) → 모습(호수, 산책로, 나무, 잔디밭, 놀이터) → 거기서 느끼는 기분·이유 → 'Yeah, that's why I love going to the park.' 마무리 문장.
공원은 '분당 중앙공원' 하나로 고정: 주말 오후 가족 산책, 아이들 자전거, 평일 저녁 혼자 걷기로 묘사·루틴 질문을 모두 커버합니다. 아침 조깅은 탄천 산책로 이야기로 따로 두세요.
경험 질문은 2년 전 봄 벚꽃 피크닉 때 딸이 처음으로 혼자 자전거를 탄 날 하나로 준비: 언제·누구와 → 무슨 일 → 기억에 남는 순간 → 느낌.
비교 질문은 '어릴 적 대전의 작은 흙 놀이터 → 지금의 크고 깨끗한 공원' 차이 2~3개(크기·시설·이용하는 사람) + 이유로 답하고, used to / these days / compared to 를 활용합니다.

expressions.en: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one.
expressions.ko: 아, 공원이요? 네, 제가 제일 좋아하는 공원에 대해 말씀드릴게요.
expressions.note: 시작 문장: 질문 키워드를 되받고 바로 '제일 좋아하는 곳' 하나로 좁히세요.

expressions.en: There's a big park near my apartment.
expressions.ko: 우리 아파트 근처에 큰 공원이 있어요.

expressions.en: It's about a 15-minute walk from my place.
expressions.note: a 15-minute walk: 숫자-minute 는 단수로 써요.

expressions.en: It has a pond, walking trails, and lots of trees.
expressions.ko: 호수랑 산책로, 그리고 나무가 많이 있어요.

expressions.en: We usually go there on weekend afternoons.
expressions.ko: 우리는 보통 주말 오후에 거기에 가요.

expressions.en: My kids ride their bikes around the pond.
expressions.ko: 우리 아이들은 호수 주변에서 자전거를 타요.

expressions.en: It's a great place to get some fresh air.
I take a walk there to clear my head after a long day.
expressions.ko: 긴 하루를 보낸 후에 머리를 식히려고 거기서 산책해요.

expressions.en: In spring, the cherry blossoms are really beautiful.
We sometimes bring a mat and have a picnic on the grass.
expressions.ko: 가끔 돗자리를 가져가서 잔디밭에서 피크닉을 해요.

expressions.en: Compared to the parks I went to as a kid, parks today are much bigger and cleaner.
expressions.ko: 제가 어릴 때 가던 공원에 비해, 요즘 공원은 훨씬 크고 깨끗해요.
expressions.note: Compared to A, B is much + 비교급

expressions.en: These days, people tend to use parks to exercise and relax.
expressions.ko: 요즘 사람들은 운동하고 쉬려고 공원을 이용하는 경향이 있어요.

expressions.en: It's like a little getaway right in the middle of the city.
expressions.ko: 도시 한가운데 있는 작은 휴양지 같아요.

expressions.en: Watching my kids run around makes all my stress melt away.
expressions.ko: 아이들이 뛰어노는 걸 보면 스트레스가 싹 녹아 없어져요.
expressions.note: make + 목적어 + 동사원형, melt away: 서서히 사라지다

expressions.en: Yeah, that's why I love going to the park.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 저는 공원 가는 걸 정말 좋아해요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to parks. Tell me about a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 공원 가는 것을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 자주 가는 공원에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 공원 이름·위치(분당 중앙공원, 집에서 걸어서 15분) → 모습(호수, 산책로, 나무, 잔디밭, 놀이터) → 계절 풍경 → 느낌 → 마무리.
묘사는 '가운데 → 주변 → 그 밖' 순서로 공간을 따라가면 길을 잃지 않습니다.
IH 이상은 봄 벚꽃·가을 단풍처럼 계절 변화를 한두 문장 더해 생생하게 만드세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one. It's Jungang Park in Bundang. It's about a 15-minute walk from my apartment. It's a big park with a pond and a lot of trees. There are walking trails, a grass field, and a playground. It's always clean and quiet. When I walk there, I feel really relaxed. I go there almost every weekend with my family. Yeah, that's my favorite park.
answers.IH: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one. It's called Jungang Park, which means Central Park, and it's in the middle of Bundang. It's only about a 15-minute walk from my apartment, so it's easy to get to. The park is really big. In the middle, there's a large pond with ducks, and there are walking trails all around it. There are tall trees everywhere, so it's nice and shady in summer. There's also a big grass field where families have picnics, and a playground for kids. In spring, the cherry blossoms along the trails are beautiful, and in fall, the leaves turn red and yellow. What I like most is that it's peaceful, even though it's in the city. Yeah, that's the park I go to most often.
answers.AL: Oh, parks? Sure, let me tell you about my favorite one. It's Jungang Park, which means Central Park, and as the name suggests, it's right in the middle of Bundang. It's about a 15-minute walk from our apartment, so we go there all the time. The first thing you notice when you walk in is how green it is. There are tall trees everywhere, and in the middle of the park there's a big pond surrounded by walking trails. On sunny days, the water sparkles and you can see ducks floating around. There's also a wide grass field where families spread out mats for picnics, a playground that my daughter loves, and a small hill with a nice view of the neighborhood. The park changes a lot with the seasons. In spring, the trails are covered in cherry blossoms, and in fall, the whole place turns red and gold. Even in winter, it's nice to walk there when everything is covered in snow. Honestly, it feels like a little getaway right in the middle of the city. After a stressful week at work, just walking there helps me breathe again. So yeah, that's the park I go to most often.

questions.en: What do you usually do when you go to the park? When do you usually go, and who do you go with?
questions.ko: 공원에 가면 주로 무엇을 하나요? 보통 언제 가고, 누구와 함께 가나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 얼마나 자주·언제(주 2회, 주말 오후) → 누구와(가족 / 가끔 혼자) → 하는 일(산책, 아이들 자전거, 벤치에서 간식, 피크닉) → 이유 → 마무리.
First / Then / After that 으로 공원에서 하는 일을 순서대로 말하세요.
'평일 저녁엔 혼자 걸으며 머리를 식힌다'는 문장으로 회사 스트레스와 연결하면 IH 이상 답변이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you about what I do at the park. I usually go to the park on weekend afternoons. I go with my family. First, we take a walk around the pond. My kids ride their bikes. Then we sit on a bench and eat some snacks. Sometimes I go there alone on weekday evenings. It helps me relax. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.
answers.IH: Sure, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park. I go to Jungang Park about twice a week. On Saturday or Sunday afternoons, I usually go with my family. We walk there together, and it takes about 15 minutes. When we arrive, my kids ride their bikes along the trail around the pond, and we walk behind them. After that, we sit on a bench and have some snacks or ice cream. When the weather is nice, we bring a mat and have a little picnic on the grass. Sometimes I also go there alone on a weekday evening after dinner. I walk slowly and listen to music, and it helps me clear my head after a long day of meetings. Yeah, that's pretty much what I do at the park.
answers.AL: Sure, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park, because it's a big part of our weekend. I go to Jungang Park about twice a week. The main visit is on Saturday or Sunday afternoon with my family. We walk there together, and by the time we arrive, the kids are already racing ahead on their bikes. While they ride around the pond, the rest of us take a slow walk and catch up on the week. After about an hour, we grab some ice cream from the convenience store near the entrance and sit on our favorite bench by the water. When the weather is really nice, we pack sandwiches and a mat and have a picnic on the grass, and my son usually ends up playing catch with me until we're both out of breath. On top of that, I sometimes go there alone on a weekday evening after dinner. I put on my earbuds, walk around the pond a few times, and let my mind go blank. After a day full of meetings and code reviews, it's the best way to recharge. So yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, what happened, and why do you still remember it?
questions.ko: 공원에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제였고, 누구와 함께 있었으며, 무슨 일이 있었고, 왜 아직도 기억하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·누구와(2년 전 봄, 가족 벚꽃 피크닉) → 무슨 일(딸이 보조바퀴 없이 자전거 연습) → 결정적 순간(몰래 손을 놓았는데 혼자 탐) → 느낌 → 마무리.
넘어지고 다시 일어나는 과정을 2~3문장으로 보여 주면 결말이 더 감동적으로 들립니다.
AL은 'to my surprise', 'Dad, look at me!' 같은 직접 인용으로 장면을 생생하게 만드세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. Two years ago in spring, my family went to Jungang Park. The cherry blossoms were beautiful. That day, my daughter was learning to ride a bike. I held the back of her bike and ran with her. Then I let go, and she rode all by herself! She was so happy, and so was I. We bought ice cream to celebrate. Yeah, that's a day I'll never forget.
answers.IH: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. I remember one time when my daughter learned to ride a bike at Jungang Park. It was two years ago in spring, and the cherry blossoms were everywhere. The four of us went there for a picnic. After lunch, my daughter wanted to try riding her bike without training wheels. She was a little scared, so I held the back of her seat and ran along with her. We tried again and again, and she fell a few times. Then, after about an hour, I let go without telling her, and she rode all the way down the trail by herself. Some people around us clapped for her. She had the biggest smile on her face. Yeah, that's why I still remember that day.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. Actually, there's one day I'll never forget. It was two springs ago, when the cherry blossoms were in full bloom. The four of us packed some kimbap and went to Jungang Park for a picnic. After lunch, my daughter announced that she was ready to ride her bike without training wheels. She was only eight, and she was pretty nervous, so I held on to the back of her seat and jogged next to her. It was harder than I thought. She wobbled, fell over a few times, and even cried once, but she kept getting back on. Then, after about an hour, I quietly let go, and to my surprise, she just kept pedaling all the way down the trail under the cherry trees. When she realized I wasn't holding on, she screamed, 'Dad, look at me!' A few people walking by actually clapped for her. My son, who usually teases her, cheered the loudest. I was out of breath and sweating, but I felt so proud. So yeah, that's why that day at the park still means so much to me.

questions.en: How are parks today different from the parks you went to when you were a child? What has changed?
questions.ko: 요즘 공원은 어렸을 때 가던 공원과 어떻게 다른가요? 무엇이 바뀌었나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 어릴 적 대전의 공원(작은 흙 놀이터, 모래밭, 그네) → 지금 분당의 공원(호수, 산책로, 자전거 도로, 운동기구) → 이용하는 사람의 변화 → 이유 → 마무리.
차이는 크기·시설·이용하는 사람 세 가지만 골라 Compared to ~, Another difference is ~ 로 연결하세요.
고난도로 이어지면 '건강과 삶의 질에 관심이 커졌다'는 이유 한 문장을 덧붙이면 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me compare them. When I was a kid, I lived in Daejeon. The park near my house was very small. It just had a sandbox and a few swings. Back then, only kids played there. Now, the parks in Bundang are much bigger and cleaner. They have walking trails, bike paths, and exercise machines. Also, many adults go to parks to exercise. I think parks are much better now. Yeah, that's how parks have changed.
answers.IH: Okay, let me compare them. I grew up in Daejeon, and the park near my house was really small. It was basically a playground with a sandbox, a slide, and a few old swings. There weren't many trees, and it got really dusty when it was windy. Compared to that, the parks I go to now are much bigger and cleaner. Jungang Park has a pond, long walking trails, bike paths, and even outdoor exercise machines. Another big difference is who uses the parks. Back then, parks were mostly for kids. These days, people of all ages use them. Older people take walks, young couples have picnics, and many people jog or walk their dogs. I think it's because people care more about their health now. Yeah, that's how parks have changed.
answers.AL: Okay, let me compare them, because the difference is pretty huge. I grew up in Daejeon in the 80s, and the park near my house was tiny. It was basically a dirt playground with a sandbox, a metal slide that got burning hot in summer, and a couple of squeaky swings. There were hardly any trees, so whenever it was windy, we came home covered in dust. Still, my friends and I played there every day until our parents called us home for dinner. Compared to that, the parks my kids go to today are on a whole different level. Jungang Park has a big pond, long walking trails, bike lanes, clean restrooms, and even outdoor exercise machines. Another big change is who uses them, and when. Back then, parks were mainly for kids, but these days, people tend to use parks to exercise and relax. You see grandparents walking, people jogging, and lots of families walking their dogs, even late in the evening. I think this change is because people care a lot more about their health and quality of life now. So yeah, parks have really changed for the better.

pronunciation.tip: 입을 크게 벌린 '아' 소리로 '판드'처럼 발음하세요. '폰드'처럼 '오'로 읽지 않도록 주의합니다.
tr은 '츄'에 가깝게 시작하고, 끝의 l은 혀끝을 윗잇몸에 대며 '츄레이얼'처럼 마무리하세요.
강세는 첫 음절 'pic'. '피크닉'의 '크'를 거의 빼고 '픽닉'처럼 짧게 말하세요.
강세는 'play'. 'ground'는 '그라운드'를 한 박자로 빠르게, 끝 d는 살짝만 내세요.
cherry는 '체리', blossom은 강세를 첫 음절에 두고 '블라썸'처럼 발음하세요.

patterns.en: There's a big park called Jungang Park near my place.
patterns.ko: 우리 집 근처에 중앙공원이라는 큰 공원이 있어요.

patterns.en: It's only a 15-minute walk from my house.
It's a big place with a pond, walking trails, and lots of tall trees.
patterns.ko: 호수와 산책로, 키 큰 나무가 많은 넓은 곳이에요.

patterns.en: I usually go to the park with my family on weekend afternoons.
patterns.ko: 저는 보통 주말 오후에 가족과 함께 공원에 가요.

patterns.en: It helps me clear my head after a long day of meetings.
patterns.ko: 하루 종일 회의를 하고 나서 머리를 식히는 데 도움이 돼요.

patterns.en: I remember one time when my daughter learned to ride a bike at the park.
patterns.ko: 딸이 공원에서 자전거 타는 법을 배웠던 때가 기억나요.

patterns.en: Compared to the tiny park in Daejeon, Jungang Park is much bigger and cleaner.
patterns.ko: 대전의 작은 공원에 비해, 중앙공원은 훨씬 크고 깨끗해요.

patterns.en: I think this change is because of people's growing interest in health.
patterns.ko: 이런 변화는 건강에 대한 사람들의 관심이 커졌기 때문이라고 생각해요.
